blocks.explanation: The full chapter architecture of Volume III, all twenty-six chapters plus appendices laid out as one map. Part I founds persistence and distinguishes becoming from living from persisting. Part II develops intent dynamics — stationary intent, the intent Lagrangian, the Hamiltonian and its co-state reading. Part III is realization theory: realization operators and their properties, multi-substrate realization across biological, digital, quantum, ecological and hybrid media, the proof of substrate independence, and TransEg, the transferred alter ego. Part IV is persistence theory proper — absolute loss of context, the invariance theorem with its uniqueness and equivalence corollaries, the persistence functional and its decay and recovery behaviour, and semantic conservation laws. Parts V to VII carry the argument out to civilization (persistent knowledge, institutions, habitats), to deep time (stellar timescales, alien semantics, cosmic persistence), and to the non-dual limit. Part VIII holds notation, proofs, connections to existing mathematics, and open problems. The closing panels give the canonical dependency graph and the axiomatic triad in which matter provides substrate, energy provides dynamics, and intent provides semantic organization.
